overall: I confirmed HEAD is exactly fe2ffd004da1a04bc4a43101a726f31f257f0632, that b9e9da7 is its ancestor, and that the tree is clean. The range is one commit, 286 insertions across nine files. I reran the three focused modules and got 132 passed; sdd.py verify reports 33 complete and 4 pending with the tree still clean afterwards; git diff --check across the range is clean; and all nine claude-architecture-review-round-*.json files validate under jsonschema.Draft202012Validator. The Git-trust mechanics are correct. _codex_shell_environment returns exactly the ten specified keys bound to the resolved delegated root, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 pin only that root as safe.directory, global and system config are nulled, system attributes, optional locks and terminal prompts are disabled, and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES is the canonical parent. I poisoned the parent environment with GIT_DIR, lowercase git_object_directory and GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES and confirmed both _git_environment helpers strip every GIT_* key case-insensitively, leaking none. _run_git and _worktree_root now prepend a command-scoped safe.directory for the resolved root ahead of the existing worktree overrides, so prior hardening is extended rather than weakened, and orchestration_evidence._git does the same independently; I recomputed repository_fingerprints under the poisoned environment and it is stable, still reports drydock-repository-fingerprint-v2, and reuse_eligible remains true, so committed-tree semantics are unchanged. I found no code path that writes Owner, global, system, repository or worktree Git configuration. The serialization is sound on native Windows: as_posix avoids backslash escaping entirely, and I parsed the generated inline table with tomllib for the real repository path containing a space, which round-tripped all ten keys with the value intact. Two things block convergence, and neither is a code defect. First, the read-only verifier's new contract exists only as prose. Nothing in process_runner.verify calls final_suite_acceptance or ProofStore.final; ProofStore appears in orchestrator.py solely to record. So the verifier no longer executes the suite and its replacement duty, auditing the exact-fingerprint record, is a model instruction rather than an enforced gate. That substitutes reading a pilot-written, user-writable, explicitly authenticated=false artifact for independent execution, and it sits in tension with the same delta's still-active clause that no cached result replaces an independent verifier. Second, the delta spec asserts an outcome nothing establishes: the scenario for Owner shell overrides says the delegated process receives only the runner's exact Git map. The test proves argv shape, not Codex behavior, and its final assertion checks a literal the test itself defined. The Codex CLI is not installed on this host, so I could verify nothing in situ about whether -c on shell_environment_policy.set replaces or merges an Owner table, nor what inherit="core" actually admits, and inherit is doing more of the real work here than the prose credits it for. Both fixes are small. I want to record what is good here, because it matters: the sandbox-SID failure and the read-only temporary-file failure were both preserved as failures with no PASS inferred, the operator guide and spec both describe the child environment as a cooperative default rather than tamper-resistant confinement, and tasks.md correctly lists a replacement full suite on a re-frozen fingerprint as pending, which is the right call because this commit changed executable-surface bytes and invalidated the prior proof. This review records evidence; it does not freeze the candidate, authenticate itself, or satisfy final verification.
blocking_concerns: The read-only verifier's proof-audit contract is instruction-only, not enforced. I grepped the verify path: neither process_runner.verify nor any runner helper calls final_suite_acceptance or ProofStore.final, and ProofStore is imported in orchestrator.py only to write a record at line 1493. The new contract removes independent execution and replaces it with the verifier reading a record that the pilot produced, that lives in a user-writable store, and that the code itself labels authenticated=false. The functions that would reject a v1, stale, intermediate, failed or fingerprint-mismatched record exist and work, but nothing calls them on this path, so a verifier that returns PASS without genuinely consulting the record, or while consulting the wrong one, violates no code gate. This is in direct tension with the still-active clause in the same delta that no cached result authorizes effects or replaces an independent verifier. Minimum correction, either of: wire the audit so the verify path refuses PASS unless final_suite_acceptance accepts the exact record against the frozen executable fingerprint, checking fingerprint_version, scope, terminal_status and executable_surface_sha256 in code rather than in prose; or remove the root cause by granting the verifier a writable temporary directory outside the repository so independent execution is restored, which preserves both read-only-to-repo and genuine independence.

The delta spec asserts Codex configuration-merge behavior that nothing in this repository proves. The scenario 'Owner shell overrides exist' states that the delegated process receives only the runner's exact Git map, and the requirement body says the runner SHALL replace inherited shell_environment_policy.set values. The runner's half is true and tested. The outcome half is not: test_codex_child_receives_exact_root_bound_git_environment proves that _codex_shell_environment returns exactly ten keys and that argv carries FIXED_CONFIG_OVERRIDES plus that inline table, which is argv shape, not CLI behavior, and its closing assertion that GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY is absent from expected_override is tautological because expected_override is built from a literal defined three lines above. The Codex CLI is absent from this host, so whether -c on a dotted table key replaces an Owner table or merges key-by-key and retains unlisted entries is unverified in every direction. This text will be merged into the living capability spec by sync, where it becomes durable normative language that a future control could be built on. Minimum correction: restate the THEN as what is proven, namely that the runner supplies its exact map as a command-scoped override and that Drydock's own Git helpers do not depend on the child environment at all, and mark replacement-versus-merge semantics as an unverified in-situ property pending a live probe.
gaps: Nothing in this review verifies live Codex behavior. The CLI is not on PATH on this host, so acceptance of the -c dotted-key inline table by the CLI's own parser, the replace-versus-merge semantics of shell_environment_policy.set, and the exact contents admitted by shell_environment_policy.inherit="core" are all unverified. My TOML conclusion is from Python's tomllib, which shows the string is syntactically valid but says nothing about the Codex parser. Every conclusion under audit points 1, 2 and 3 is configuration-shape proof only. A single live probe that dumps the delegated child's effective environment would convert most of this from claim to evidence.

The prose leans on shell_environment_policy.set while shell_environment_policy.inherit="core" is doing the heavier protective work. The set table pins ten variables; it does not by itself prevent GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR or GIT_NAMESPACE from reaching the child. What excludes those is inherit="core", pinned in FIXED_CONFIG_OVERRIDES, whose membership is Codex-defined and unverified here. The operator guide and spec should credit inherit explicitly so a future reader does not weaken it believing set is sufficient.

GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES carries a single value today, so the platform list separator is never exercised. Git uses semicolons on Windows and colons elsewhere, and the current code performs no joining. That is fine as written and brittle the moment a second ceiling is added; a comment or a helper would prevent a silent portability bug later.

The closing assertion in the new argv test checks the test's own literal rather than production output. The equality assertion above it does carry real weight, including proving the monkeypatched poison does not enter the map, so this is redundancy rather than a false pass. It should still be replaced by an assertion against _codex_shell_environment_override output so the test reads as strongly as it actually is.
risks: Whatever fix is chosen for the verifier must not silently re-grant write access to the repository. The original failure is real: pytest cannot create temporary files inside the native read-only boundary. Granting a writable temporary directory outside the repository preserves both properties; widening the sandbox to workspace-write would trade the boundary for convenience and should be refused.

Making the verifier depend on a proof record raises the value of tampering with that record. The store is user-writable by design and labels itself authenticated=false, which was acceptable while it only accelerated intermediate work. If it becomes an input to final acceptance, that non-authentication needs restating at the point of use, not only at the point of storage.

This commit changed executable-surface bytes, so the previously recorded full-suite proof no longer binds the current fingerprint. tasks.md correctly lists a re-freeze and one replacement full required suite as pending. That discipline is right and should not be shortcut by reusing the earlier record.

The two operational failures behind this change, the sandbox-SID dubious-ownership error and the read-only temporary-file mismatch, were both preserved as failures with no PASS inferred, and the timed-out verifier attempt was recorded rather than retried into a verdict. That is the behavior the packet exists to produce and it is worth noting as evidence the governance is working rather than being worked around.

The cooperative-default framing in the operator guide and delta spec is accurate and should survive sync unchanged. It is the sentence that keeps the injected Git environment from being mistaken for confinement.

Carried and unchanged: the capability still spans stacked unsynced deltas so supersession reasoning stays manual until archive, default phase and run envelopes remain uncalibrated, and fixed-root mutation containment remains unexercised for this work because the pilot edited the scoped Owner checkout directly after the runner failures.
required_changes: Enforce the verifier's proof audit in code rather than prose: refuse PASS unless final_suite_acceptance accepts the exact record against the frozen executable fingerprint, validating fingerprint_version, scope, terminal_status and executable_surface_sha256; or restore independent execution by giving the verifier a writable temporary directory outside the repository.

Restate the 'Owner shell overrides exist' scenario so its THEN describes only what is proven, and record replace-versus-merge semantics for shell_environment_policy.set as an unverified in-situ property.

Credit shell_environment_policy.inherit="core" explicitly in the spec and operator guide as the mechanism that excludes unlisted inherited GIT_* variables, so it is not weakened later on the belief that the set table is sufficient.
Replace the tautological GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY assertion with one made against _codex_shell_environment_override output.

Run one live probe that captures the delegated child's effective environment under an Owner shell_environment_policy.set table, and record the result as the in-situ evidence this review could not obtain.
